video.title: It Took Me 20 Years to Master Business. You Get It In 25 Minutes

summary: David Heacock, founder of Filterbuy (US air filter manufacturer, claimed ~150,000 filters/day and ~$25M/month revenue), shares five stages of building a boring business: commit long enough to learn, fund the constraint, build systems that preserve judgment, don't diversify before the core is ready, and build resilience and legacy. He recounts leaving Goldman, buying a declining $300k/yr business with debt, taking $50k salary for 7.5 years, and losing millions in 2021 by launching a freight company and buying an HVAC business while the core was doubling. Key takeaway: do the work yourself first, turn judgment into systems, and put capital into the core constraint rather than diversifying early.

speakers.name: David Heacock
speakers.description: Founder/CEO of Filterbuy, ex-Goldman Sachs options trader, building Filterbuy Ventures

ideas.name: Filterbuy: direct-to-consumer pleated air filter manufacturing
ideas.one_liner: Manufacture pleated air filters in the US in many sizes and ship direct to customers with same-day shipping.
ideas.business_model: One-off and repeat product sales shipped direct to end customers across multiple channels
ideas.customer: Homeowners and other buyers needing replacement HVAC air filters (direct and across different channels)
ideas.problem: Customers keep needing filters in many sizes and the existing customer experience was not particularly good
ideas.offer: Made-in-US pleated filters across about 11,000-12,000 SKUs, ~4.5 filters per box, same-day ship for orders before ~2pm cut-off

pricing.notes: Speaker said he was wrong about pricing early on; no price figures given

acquisition_channels.details: Poured excess capital and energy into marketing when sales were the bottleneck; sells direct to customer and across different channels. Specific channels not stated.

ideas.delivery: Nine locations across US and Canada, three manufacturing facilities supplying six others; under two weeks of finished goods inventory; production schedule initially done by hand by the founder, then a tool, then a trained production manager; over a thousand employees.
unit_economics_claims: Bought business making ~$300k/yr and declining with $1.5M debt
ideas.startup_cost: $1.5M debt to acquire an existing business making ~$300k/yr

acquisition.how: Direct online sales; marketing details not stated but ecommerce marketing is largely automatable.

onboarding.how: Ecommerce checkout with size lookup requires little human involvement.

delivery.how: Physical manufacturing, warehousing and shipping across multiple plants and over a thousand staff.

support.how: Order and sizing queries can be agent-handled; returns and damaged goods need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Product is universal, but UK uses different filter formats and far fewer ducted forced-air homes, and the venture needs heavy capital and factories.

risks: Very little margin for error in production planning with low inventory

tactics.name: Do it manually, build tool, hand off, then iterate
steps: Do the critical weekly job yourself manually longer than feels comfortable to learn the tradeoffs
Build a rough tool that encodes how you make the decision
Train a person to run the tool daily without you
Watch, give feedback and repeat until they outperform you

quote.text: I would do the job myself manually long enough that I understood not just the steps, but the tradeoffs that I was making
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Fund the current constraint
steps: Identify whether sales or operations is currently the bottleneck
Put available cash and attention into that constraint
Swing back when the other side becomes the bottleneck
Keep experiments small (small cost, about a week of attention)

quote.text: you just have to follow whichever half of the business is breaking
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Four-question diversification test
steps: Does the core have a management team that can operate it?
Do you have a real framework or advantage that transfers to the new area?
Does the new initiative reinforce the long-term vision rather than satisfy novelty?
Is the core already receiving all the capital and attention it can productively use?

quote.text: the core business is already receiving all the capital and attention it can productively use
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Choose a boring product by durability
steps: Shortlist products you can make competitively locally and sell direct
Ask what will not change in 10-20 years
Prefer products with a mediocre existing customer experience

quote.text: I chose based on which boring product would still exist in 20 years.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tools_mentioned.purpose: Automates daily production plan across plants

tools_mentioned.name: AI development tooling

warnings.warning: Diversifying (freight + HVAC) while the core was doubling cost millions and years of cleanup.

quote.text: It cost us millions of dollars and years of cleanup.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

warnings.warning: Delegating before you've figured out the work yourself leaves you unable to judge or give feedback.

quote.text: you hire a junior marketer before you know what good marketing for your company looks like
quote.speaker: David Heacock

warnings.warning: Systems built so you can stop paying attention break when reality changes.

quote.text: A system built so you can stop paying attention will usually break the first time reality changes on you.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

warnings.warning: Estate planning gets more expensive after value is created; do it early.

lessons.lesson: Commitment and long runway let you afford to be wrong; keeping personal pay low funded years of mistakes.

quote.text: When you have a runway, you can afford to be wrong.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Always preserving options has a cost; building something meaningful requires closing doors.
Pick boring products whose demand will persist so knowledge compounds over decades.

quote.text: the knowledge within them compounds
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: A real system preserves judgment, not just a checklist of activities.

quote.text: A checklist documents activity while a real system preserves judgment.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Momentum is not proof you can do anything; put extra capital into the core while it can still absorb it.
Aim for a resilient company rather than one that needs no founder; absence is not the goal.

quote.text: absence was never the objective. Resilience was.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

lessons.lesson: Staying private and self-controlled allows decade-long thinking instead of quarterly pressure.
Be willing to rebuild systems as technology like AI changes what is possible.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator at large scale with some specific figures, but the advice is reflective and largely qualitative, with no unit economics, pricing or acquisition specifics, and figures are unverified.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes Filterbuy Ventures and his own YouTube content (first-million video); personal brand building.
